messages:
maria: handing off OptKit prioritization for sprint planning. need final ordering + concrete launch criteria by EOD so eng can size. i did a quick gut pass and am inclined to order: batching -> caching -> quantization (8-bit). please do a quick RICE pass and call out blockers. doc: https://confluence.redwood/optkit/prio (draft)

ajay: agree batching usually gives the best immediate unit-cost wins for gen workloads. did a rough RICE draft below — numbers are rough, plz sanity-check:
```
feature   reach impact confidence effort  RICE
batching    8     6     0.8       3     (8*6*0.8)/3 = 12.8
caching     6     5     0.7       3     (6*5*0.7)/3 = 7.0
quant(8-bit)4     5     0.6       5     (4*5*0.6)/5 = 2.4
``` 
batching and caching numbers depend a lot on workload mix; quantization has high engineering/quality cost so lower RICE for MVP.

sophie: note from customer validation: enterprise customer "NorthStar" asked specifically for 4-bit support on Llama2-70B. that's a big ask and will increase QA overhead. recommend we treat 4-bit as enterprise-only/backlog and focus on 8-bit for general availability.

leo: infra notes — caching requires KV integration, eviction policies, and per-tenant metrics. effort is likely E3 not E2. also we need rollout hooks: feature flags + metric windows. for batching, we need to confirm autoscaler behavior under bursty traffic.

maria: proposed launch criteria (draft):
1) Batching: demonstrate >=20% unit cost reduction on representative gen workloads with P95 latency <= 1.2x baseline and no increase in error rate. load test + canary for 48h.
2) Caching: prefix/KV cache with hit-rate >= 35% on prefix-heavy customers, correctness/regression tests for output equality (or documented divergence), and observability (per-tenant hit/miss + cost delta).
3) Quantization (8-bit): end-to-end quality evals with >=95% pass on curated prompt suite, regression checks vs FP16 on top-1 tokens, and explicit gating to Dedicated/Private if quality isn't met. 4-bit remains enterprise backlog.

ajay: i'll update the doc with the RICE table and add rough engineering estimates. question for product: do we want to prioritize caching before quant if caching effort is actually lower? current ordering flexible if RICE flips.

sophie: i can own quant quality evals but need the eval dataset and 2 reviewers for labeling edge cases. i'll add a quick rubric and planned dataset to the doc. also recommend adding customer-facing release notes for potential quality deltas.

leo: add rollback policy to launch criteria: automatic fallback to FP16/dedicated variant on any latency/regression spike > 10% and killswitch for affected tenant. also include smoke tests in CI that run small regen checks.

maria: thanks all. next steps: @ajay update RICE+estimates, @sophie own evals + rubric, @leo add rollout/rollback steps in infra section. i'll lock provisional roadmap: batching -> caching -> 8-bit quant; 4-bit enterprise backlog. will update the roadmap board and tag eng leads for planning. :rocket:

deploy-bot: document uploaded: /confluence/optkit/prio_v3 (sha: ab12cd)

maria: quick follow-up — any blockers for shipping batching in the next 6-week sprint? need to know if we must split into smaller sub-features. :thinking:

ajay: main blocker is autoscaler + sequence-length variability. proposes splitting: (A) continuous batching runtime + metrics, (B) autoscale tuning + policies. A can ship earlier as internal feature flag.

sophie: will start running sample evals on batching to check if batching changes generation characteristics on our prompt sets.

leo: i'll scope KV infra work for caching and provide E2 estimates by EOD tomorrow. can we push a quick tech spike for autoscaler changes this week? that will reduce uncertainty for sprint planning. :+1:
